guidelines.title: filled next outline this page
guidelines.rule: Standard (filled) for actions that go to a next step. Outline for actions that happen on the current page. Unstyled only for less important actions that may look like links.
pass_when: Next-step actions are filled; same-page actions are outline; unstyled is only for less important link-like actions.
fail_when: Filled used for a same-page action, outline used as the next-step control, or unstyled used as the primary next step.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Actions one-primary / distinctive-primary as this row.

guidelines.title: real button with type space vs enter
guidelines.rule: Use a real `<button>` with `type` set (`submit` / `button` / `reset`; default is submit). Do not use `<a>` or `<div>` as the only control. Space triggers a button; Enter triggers a link — do not style links as buttons without that difference.
pass_when: The control is `<button>` with an explicit `type`. Links are not styled as the only button control.
fail_when: `<a>` or `<div>` is the only control, or `type` is omitted on a non-submit button so it submits.

guidelines.title: dont split phone ssn card
guidelines.rule: Do not split phone, SSN, or credit-card numbers into separate fields. One input; segmented fields force meaningless labels for AT. Distinct from GOV.UK three-field dates.
pass_when: Phone, SSN, and card number are each one field.
fail_when: Those numbers are split across multiple fields.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Memorable date three fields as this row; input-mask (skipped as NN/g).

guidelines.title: forms simple vertical stack
guidelines.rule: Forms stay a simple vertical stack. Do not rearrange controls with CSS (AT follows HTML order). Vertical is the layout for limited-vision left-to-right scanning.
pass_when: Controls follow source order in a vertical stack.
fail_when: CSS reorders fields away from HTML order, or a multi-column scramble that AT does not match.

guidelines.title: character count brevity or legal
guidelines.rule: Character count only for brevity or a legal cap — not to paper over backend field limits (raise the limit). Skip if length is implied (phone/zip) or if well over 99% of users will never hit the cap (e.g. address at 250). Provide a non-JS backup message. Dual-cite GOV.UK raise-backend + no-maxlength-truncate vs USWDS using `maxlength` for the component. No winner on truncate.
pass_when: Count is shown only for brevity or a legal cap; backend limit is raised rather than used as a fake cap; implied-length and never-hit caps omit the count; a non-JS backup message exists.
fail_when: Count papers over a short backend limit; or count on phone/zip / an address field almost nobody will hit.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A winner that bans or requires `maxlength`.

guidelines.title: search min 27 chars persist query
guidelines.rule: Search field as wide as possible, minimum 27 characters (Romance languages ~20% longer). Preload the original terms in the results search box. Magnifying glass is enough visually if “Search” remains for AT.
pass_when: Field is ≥27 characters wide; results page still shows the query; accessible name remains “Search” if the visible label is icon-only.
fail_when: Narrower than 27 characters; query not persisted on results; icon-only with no AT name.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Placeholder-as-label; advanced search as default (next row).

guidelines.title: homepage search box not link
guidelines.rule: Home page: search box, not a search link. Advanced search is not the default (most people use one or two terms; advanced as default increases mistakes). Tiny/single-page sites may omit search.
pass_when: Home offers a search field (unless the site is tiny/single-page and omits search); default search is simple, not advanced.
fail_when: Home search is only a link to another page, or advanced search is the default.

guidelines.title: alert first word is type
guidelines.rule: First word is the type: Informative / Warning / Success / Error / Emergency (or a more precise first word such as “Announcement”). Heading ≤1 line. Extra detail in the body, not a second heading line. Users must not rely on colour or icon alone.
pass_when: Heading starts with the type (or a more precise first word), stays on one line, and meaning is not colour/icon-only.
fail_when: Type is only an icon/colour; heading wraps to a second line of detail.

guidelines.title: alerts dont blame name next step
guidelines.rule: Don’t blame the user; name the next step. Polite; include how to recover. Educational material is allowed because people will read an error that unblocks them. Don’t notify off the current goal. Destructive work → confirmation modal, not an alert.
pass_when: Copy is polite, names recovery, stays on the current goal; destructive actions use a confirmation modal.
fail_when: Blame-the-user copy; no next step; alert used instead of a destructive confirmation; notification unrelated to the current goal.

guidelines.title: dont hide then reveal alerts
guidelines.rule: Don’t hide-then-reveal alerts in the DOM — older AT can still perceive visually hidden messages that are not currently applicable.
pass_when: Inapplicable alerts are not left visually hidden in the DOM.
fail_when: Alerts stay in the DOM as visually hidden until “revealed.”
guidelines.do_not_claim: Site-alert unused-remove (`display:none`) from the first-pass catalog as this row.

guidelines.title: site alert dont stack dont panic
guidelines.rule: One full-width site alert near the top. Do not stack. Multiple messages = a list of links inside a single site alert. Positioning already gives weight; do not use heavy red/orange panic colour. Dual-cite GOV.UK notification banner and System status: sitewide static, never form validation, never stacked.
pass_when: At most one sitewide static site alert; extra messages are links inside it; not used for form/task validation; colour is not panic-red/orange as the only weight.
fail_when: Stacked site alerts; site alert used as field/page form validation; or panic colour as the only signal.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Page alert type-word (`uswds.alert-first-word-is-type`); live system-status toasts.

guidelines.title: date picker when weekday always type
guidelines.rule: Date picker only when weekday / scheduling context helps. Always allow typing. Birthdays and other well-known dates use memorable date fields. Hint `mm/dd/yyyy`. Do not auto-submit on picking a day. Dual-cite GOV.UK three-field memorable date (no auto-tab) and USWDS month=select vs three text fields — both pass if labeled, no auto-advance, not `type=number`. Do not pick a house month control.
pass_when: Well-known dates are memorable fields (typed); picker is optional for scheduling and typing still works; no auto-submit; no auto-advance; day/year not `type=number`.
fail_when: Birthday-only calendar with no typing; auto-submit on pick; auto-advance; `type=number` day/year.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A winner between month-select and three text fields.

guidelines.title: banner gov mil https every page
guidelines.rule: Unaltered .gov/.mil + HTTPS copy on every page, after skipnav. Only on official .gov/.mil with HTTPS; never on .com/.org or test sites. Spanish copy on Spanish sites; `.mil` copy on `.mil`. Do not leave `aria-hidden="true"` on banner content in markup (JS sets it).
pass_when: Official .gov/.mil HTTPS sites show the unaltered TLD/HTTPS banner on every page after skipnav; language/TLD copy matches the site; banner content is not `aria-hidden` in the markup.
fail_when: Banner on .com/.org or test; customized TLD text; missing on inner pages; or `aria-hidden="true"` left on banner content in markup.
guidelines.do_not_claim: This as an Open UX rule for non-government products; Canada signature / NSW hero as the same rule.

guidelines.title: identifier required links not footer dup
guidelines.rule: Identifier holds the required federal links — don’t duplicate them in the site footer. Parent agency (highest in the hierarchy), not the product logo. Multiple parents/logos in hierarchical order, highest first. Omit identifier logo if it duplicates the footer agency mark. Entire component; no deleted required links.
pass_when: Required links live in the identifier once (not also in the footer); parent agency is highest in hierarchy; product logo is not used as the identifier mark; required links are not deleted.
fail_when: Required links duplicated in the footer; product logo in the identifier; required links omitted.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Identifier darker-than-footer (next row) as this links rule; Canada GC signature as a merge.

guidelines.title: identifier darker than footer
guidelines.rule: Identifier darker than the footer (grade 80+ / black). Primary or base family, darker than the preceding section, anchored at the bottom so it is not another footer stripe.
pass_when: Identifier is darker than the preceding footer section (primary/base grade 80+ or black) and sits at the bottom.
fail_when: Identifier matches the footer stripe or sits mid-page as another footer band.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Required-links placement as this colour row.
